Time limits of a call to the module

module_timeouts.Rd

Five minutes for the whole call and thirty seconds to connect, the connection taking in name resolution and the TLS handshake as libcurl counts it.

Usage

module_timeouts()

Value

A list with total and connect, in seconds.

Details

The whole call is the longest thing the module is asked: the read of state of a whole instance, which step 3b of the round makes on every production, and a write of many rows. Measured on 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-11, the observer read all nine instances it reaches whole, about 18,450 pairs, Key Vault included, in about 75 seconds; the largest instance alone took less. Five minutes is four times the whole fleet. A write that runs out of time may have been carried out, so the limit errs long rather than short: a write too slow for it is a row that converges one round later, and its access message is lost (see mail_round()), while an instance that never answers costs at most two waits per round. One that answers reads and hangs on writes costs a wait for every batch it is sent, one per project.

Connecting does nothing on the instance, so a short limit costs no write. Thirty seconds is far above a connection inside the network and well below libcurl's default of 300 seconds.
